schemas.name: Library
schemas.schema_description:
A small library lending database.

The members table stores people registered at the library: member_id (a unique identifier), full_name (the member's full name), and join_date (the date the member registered).

The books table stores books owned by the library: book_id (a unique identifier), title (the book's title), and genre (the book's genre).

The loans table records a member borrowing a book: loan_id (a unique identifier), member_id (the member who borrowed the book), book_id (the book that was borrowed), loan_date (the date borrowed), and return_date (the date returned, empty if not yet returned).
schemas.constraints:
Primary keys: members.member_id, books.book_id, loans.loan_id.
Foreign keys: loans.member_id references members.member_id; loans.book_id references books.book_id.

questions.nl_question: List the full names of members who joined in 2023.
questions.gold_query: SELECT full_name FROM members WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM join_date) = 2023

submissions.submission_query: SELECT full_name FROM members WHERE join_date BETWEEN DATE '2023-01-01' AND DATE '2023-12-31'
submissions.human_reason: Equivalent date-range filter; returns the same members as the gold query.

submissions.submission_query: SELECT full_name FROM membrs WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM join_date) = 2023
submissions.human_reason: The table name 'membrs' does not exist in the schema.

submissions.submission_query: SELECT full_name FROM members WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM join_date) = 2022
submissions.human_reason: Filters on the year 2022 instead of 2023, so it returns the wrong members.

submissions.submission_query: SELECT m.full_name FROM members m WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM m.join_date) = 2023
submissions.human_reason: Same logic as the gold query, only with a table alias; result is identical.

submissions.submission_query: SELECT member_id FROM members WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM join_date) = 2023
submissions.human_reason: Projects member_id instead of the requested full_name.

questions.nl_question: How many books has each member borrowed? Show the member's name and the count.
questions.gold_query: SELECT m.full_name, COUNT(*) FROM members m JOIN loans l ON l.member_id = m.member_id GROUP BY m.full_name

submissions.submission_query: SELECT m.full_name, COUNT(*) FROM members m JOIN loans l ON l.member_id = m.member_id GROUP BY m.full_name
submissions.human_reason: Matches the gold query exactly.

submissions.submission_query: SELECT m.full_name, COUNT(*) FROM members m JOIN loans l ON l.member_id = m.member_id
submissions.human_reason: Aggregate with a non-aggregated column and no GROUP BY; Oracle rejects this (ORA-00937).

submissions.submission_query: SELECT m.full_name, COUNT(*) FROM members m JOIN loans l ON l.member_id = m.member_id GROUP BY m.member_id, m.full_name
submissions.human_reason: Grouping by member_id as well as full_name is equivalent here and safer against duplicate names; same counts.

submissions.submission_query: SELECT m.full_name, COUNT(*) FROM members m LEFT JOIN loans l ON l.member_id = m.member_id GROUP BY m.full_name
submissions.human_reason: The LEFT JOIN adds members with no loans and COUNT(*) reports 1 for them instead of 0.

questions.nl_question: List the titles of books that have never been borrowed.
questions.gold_query: SELECT b.title FROM books b WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM loans l WHERE l.book_id = b.book_id)

submissions.submission_query: SELECT b.title FROM books b LEFT JOIN loans l ON l.book_id = b.book_id WHERE l.loan_id IS NULL
submissions.human_reason: Anti-join written as a LEFT JOIN with an IS NULL test; returns the same titles as the gold query.

submissions.submission_query: SELECT title FROM books WHERE book_id NOT IN (SELECT book_id FROM loans)
submissions.human_reason: loans.book_id is a NOT NULL foreign key, so NOT IN is safe here and equivalent to the gold query.

submissions.submission_query: SELECT title FROM books WHERE book_id NOT IN (SELECT book_id FROM loan)
submissions.human_reason: The subquery reads from 'loan'; the schema defines the table as 'loans'.

submissions.submission_query: SELECT b.title FROM books b JOIN loans l ON l.book_id = b.book_id WHERE l.return_date IS NULL
submissions.human_reason: Returns books that are currently out on loan, not books that were never borrowed.

questions.nl_question: Show the number of books in each genre, ordered from most to fewest.
questions.gold_query: SELECT genre, COUNT(*) FROM books GROUP BY genre ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC

submissions.submission_query: SELECT genre, COUNT(*) AS book_count FROM books GROUP BY genre ORDER BY book_count DESC
submissions.human_reason: Same grouping and ordering as the gold query; only adds a column alias.

submissions.submission_query: SELECT genre, COUNT(*) FROM books GROUP BY genre ORDER BY COUNT(*) ASC
submissions.human_reason: Orders from fewest to most; the question asks for most to fewest.

submissions.submission_query: SELECT genre, COUNT(*) FROM books ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC
submissions.human_reason: Aggregate with a non-aggregated column and no GROUP BY; Oracle rejects this (ORA-00937).

submissions.submission_query: SELECT genre, COUNT(*) FROM books GROUP BY genre ORDER BY genre DESC
submissions.human_reason: Orders alphabetically by genre rather than by the count.

questions.nl_question: List the full names of members who have borrowed a book but have not returned it.
questions.gold_query: SELECT DISTINCT m.full_name FROM members m JOIN loans l ON l.member_id = m.member_id WHERE l.return_date IS NULL

submissions.submission_query: SELECT m.full_name FROM members m WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM loans l WHERE l.member_id = m.member_id AND l.return_date IS NULL)
submissions.human_reason: EXISTS returns each qualifying member once, the same set as the gold query's DISTINCT join.

submissions.submission_query: SELECT DISTINCT m.full_name FROM members m JOIN loans l ON l.member_id = m.member_id WHERE l.return_date = NULL
submissions.human_reason: Parses, but '= NULL' is never true in Oracle, so the query always returns no rows; IS NULL is required.

submissions.submission_query: SELECT DISTINCT m.full_name FROM members m JOIN loans l ON l.member_id = m.membr_id WHERE l.return_date IS NULL
submissions.human_reason: The join references m.membr_id; the members table has no such column.

submissions.submission_query: SELECT DISTINCT m.full_name FROM members m JOIN loans l ON l.member_id = m.member_id WHERE l.return_date IS NOT NULL
submissions.human_reason: Returns members who have returned their books, the opposite of what the question asks.

questions.nl_question: Which members joined before 2023 and have never borrowed a book?
questions.gold_query: SELECT m.full_name FROM members m WHERE m.join_date < DATE '2023-01-01' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM loans l WHERE l.member_id = m.member_id)

submissions.submission_query: SELECT m.full_name FROM members m LEFT JOIN loans l ON l.member_id = m.member_id WHERE m.join_date < DATE '2023-01-01' AND l.loan_id IS NULL
submissions.human_reason: Anti-join written as a LEFT JOIN with an IS NULL test, same date bound; equivalent to the gold query.

submissions.submission_query: SELECT m.full_name FROM members m WHERE m.join_date <= DATE '2023-01-01' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM loans l WHERE l.member_id = m.member_id)
submissions.human_reason: Uses <= so members who joined on 2023-01-01 are included; the question says before 2023.

submissions.submission_query: SELECT m.full_name FROM members m WHERE m.join_date < DATE '2023-01-01' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM loans l WHERE l.member = m.member_id)
submissions.human_reason: The subquery references l.member; the loans table has no such column.

submissions.submission_query: SELECT m.full_name FROM members m WHERE m.join_date < DATE '2023-01-01'
submissions.human_reason: Drops the never-borrowed condition and returns every member who joined before 2023.

questions.nl_question: For each genre, show the genre and how many times books in that genre have been borrowed.
questions.gold_query: SELECT b.genre, COUNT(*) FROM books b JOIN loans l ON l.book_id = b.book_id GROUP BY b.genre

submissions.submission_query: SELECT b.genre, COUNT(*) AS loan_count FROM books b JOIN loans l ON l.book_id = b.book_id GROUP BY b.genre
submissions.human_reason: Same join and grouping as the gold query; only adds a column alias.

submissions.submission_query: SELECT b.genre, COUNT(*) FROM loans l JOIN books b ON b.book_id = l.book_id GROUP BY b.genre
submissions.human_reason: The join is written from the other side, which does not change the result.

submissions.submission_query: SELECT b.genre, COUNT(DISTINCT b.book_id) FROM books b JOIN loans l ON l.book_id = b.book_id GROUP BY b.genre
submissions.human_reason: Counts how many distinct books in the genre were borrowed, not how many times they were borrowed.

submissions.submission_query: SELECT b.genre, b.title, COUNT(*) FROM books b JOIN loans l ON l.book_id = b.book_id GROUP BY b.genre
submissions.human_reason: b.title is selected but not grouped or aggregated; Oracle rejects this (ORA-00979).

schemas.name: Store
schemas.schema_description:
A small online store database.

The customers table stores registered buyers: customer_id (a unique identifier), name (the customer's name), city (the city they live in), and signup_date (the date they registered).

The products table stores items for sale: product_id (a unique identifier), name (the product's name), category (the product's category), and unit_price (the current list price).

The orders table records an order placed by a customer: order_id (a unique identifier), customer_id (the customer who placed it), order_date (the date it was placed), and status (the order's status).

The order_items table records one product line within an order: order_item_id (a unique identifier), order_id (the order it belongs to), product_id (the product ordered), quantity (how many units), and unit_price (the price charged per unit on this order, which may differ from the product's current list price).
schemas.constraints:
Primary keys: customers.customer_id, products.product_id, orders.order_id, order_items.order_item_id.
Foreign keys: orders.customer_id references customers.customer_id; order_items.order_id references orders.order_id; order_items.product_id references products.product_id.

questions.nl_question: List the names of customers who live in Berlin.
questions.gold_query: SELECT name FROM customers WHERE city = 'Berlin'

submissions.submission_query: SELECT c.name FROM customers c WHERE c.city = 'Berlin'
submissions.human_reason: Same filter and projection as the gold query, only with a table alias.

submissions.submission_query: SELECT name FROM customer WHERE city = 'Berlin'
submissions.human_reason: The FROM clause names 'customer'; the schema defines the table as 'customers'.

submissions.submission_query: SELECT name FROM customers WHERE city = 'berlin'
submissions.human_reason: String comparison is case sensitive in Oracle, so 'berlin' matches no rows.

submissions.submission_query: SELECT city FROM customers WHERE city = 'Berlin'
submissions.human_reason: Projects city instead of the requested customer name.

questions.nl_question: How many orders has each customer placed? Show the customer name and the count.
questions.gold_query: SELECT c.name, COUNT(*) FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.name

submissions.submission_query: SELECT c.name, COUNT(*) FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.name
submissions.human_reason: Grouping by customer_id as well as name is equivalent here and safer against duplicate names.

submissions.submission_query: SELECT c.name, COUNT(*) FROM customers c, orders o GROUP BY c.name
submissions.human_reason: No join condition, so this cross joins and counts every order against every customer.

submissions.submission_query: SELECT c.name, COUNT(*) FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.custmer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.name
submissions.human_reason: The join references o.custmer_id; the orders table has no such column.

submissions.submission_query: SELECT c.name, COUNT(*) FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.name HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
submissions.human_reason: Adds a HAVING filter the question does not ask for, dropping customers with a single order.

questions.nl_question: Show the total quantity ordered for each product, from highest to lowest.
questions.gold_query: SELECT p.name, SUM(i.quantity) FROM products p JOIN order_items i ON i.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.name ORDER BY SUM(i.quantity) DESC

submissions.submission_query: SELECT p.name, SUM(i.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM products p JOIN order_items i ON i.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.name ORDER BY total_quantity DESC
submissions.human_reason: Ordering by the select-list alias is allowed in ORDER BY; same result as the gold query.

submissions.submission_query: SELECT p.name, COUNT(*) FROM products p JOIN order_items i ON i.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.name ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC
submissions.human_reason: Counts order lines per product instead of summing the quantity ordered.

submissions.submission_query: SELECT p.name, SUM(i.quantiy) FROM products p JOIN order_items i ON i.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.name ORDER BY SUM(i.quantiy) DESC
submissions.human_reason: Misspelled column i.quantiy; the order_items table has quantity.

submissions.submission_query: SELECT p.name, SUM(i.quantity) FROM products p JOIN order_items i ON i.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.name ORDER BY 3 DESC
submissions.human_reason: ORDER BY 3 names a third select-list item that does not exist; Oracle rejects this (ORA-01785).

questions.nl_question: List the names of products that have never been ordered.
questions.gold_query: SELECT p.name FROM products p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items i WHERE i.product_id = p.product_id)

submissions.submission_query: SELECT p.name FROM products p LEFT JOIN order_items i ON i.product_id = p.product_id WHERE i.order_item_id IS NULL
submissions.human_reason: Anti-join written as a LEFT JOIN with an IS NULL test; same products as the gold query.

submissions.submission_query: SELECT name FROM products WHERE product_id NOT IN (SELECT product_id FROM order_items)
submissions.human_reason: order_items.product_id is a NOT NULL foreign key, so NOT IN is safe and equivalent here.

submissions.submission_query: SELECT name FROM products WHERE product_id NOT IN (SELECT product_id FROM orders)
submissions.human_reason: The subquery selects product_id from orders; that column lives on order_items, not orders.

submissions.submission_query: SELECT p.name FROM products p JOIN order_items i ON i.product_id = p.product_id WHERE i.quantity = 0
submissions.human_reason: Returns products ordered with a zero quantity, not products that were never ordered.

questions.nl_question: Which customers have spent more than 500 in total? Show the customer name and the total spent.
questions.gold_query: SELECT c.name, SUM(i.quantity * i.unit_price) FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY c.name HAVING SUM(i.quantity * i.unit_price) > 500

submissions.submission_query: SELECT c.name, SUM(i.unit_price * i.quantity) FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY c.name HAVING SUM(i.unit_price * i.quantity) > 500
submissions.human_reason: Same joins written in a different order and the factors swapped; identical result.

submissions.submission_query: SELECT c.name, SUM(i.quantity * i.unit_price) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY c.name HAVING total_spent > 500
submissions.human_reason: Oracle does not allow a select-list alias in HAVING; total_spent is not in scope there (ORA-00904).

submissions.submission_query: SELECT c.name, SUM(i.quantity * i.unit_price) FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.order_id WHERE SUM(i.quantity * i.unit_price) > 500 GROUP BY c.name
submissions.human_reason: An aggregate cannot appear in WHERE; Oracle rejects this (ORA-00934).

submissions.submission_query: SELECT c.name, SUM(i.quantity * p.unit_price) FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products p ON p.product_id = i.product_id GROUP BY c.name HAVING SUM(i.quantity * p.unit_price) > 500
submissions.human_reason: Uses the product's current list price instead of the price charged on the order line.
